tooltip.unfading_dawn.charm.pike_tooth: A blow in the back is %s%% harder
tooltip.unfading_dawn.charm.tide_pearl: Health comes back by itself: half a heart every %s s

screen.unfading_dawn.hearth.charm.hint: Take a charm in your hand and right click
Mind your feet, they lie here. They did lie. I sing them to their rest and they get up. So I sing again.
Have you seen the dawn over the Stockade? The Founder holds it, so the night cannot reach us. And down here it is night. So we have not earned it yet.
If you want to set a candle, set one. A stub is like a soul: it burns lower, but it burns.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.graved: I sang the Gravedigger to his rest. The first in all this time who lay down after and stays down.
He did not bury, you know, he raised. Who will raise them now? ...Forgive me. I do not know whether to be glad.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.chapla: The Chaplain gave me candles from the cathedral, lit from the Last Light. He said: the dawn will come, only keep standing.
You laid him down? Well. Then I am the only one standing now.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.mother: They say she was taken down, out on the Mire. The one who said the day must end. Rightly hanged, everybody said so.
I set a candle because she was hanged. Not for her rest: she had none. Now I do not know what to set it for.
The Elder lies down? The Unsleeping used to come to me for candles, before they went off to the firwood. They took more than a night can burn.
I wondered at the time what night they meant to wait out.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.coming: You killed something under the ground, you say? Do not tell me. I do not want to know what is under us.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.starte: Do you hear? Something knocks under the ground. Like a finger on a coffin lid from inside... No. Steadier. Like a clock.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.raised: A tower has stood up in the middle of the market. I will not go in. There is a bell up there.
A bell is a burial song for everyone at once. I could never sing so many on my own.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.seat.0: The dawn stands as it stood. So he sits up there again. Or someone in his place.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.idle.0: I sang three to their rest today. Two are up already.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.idle.1: If someone of yours lies here, tell me the name. I remember everyone here. Only not my own.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.idle.2: We have night because all the dawn is up there. There was not enough for everyone.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.idle.3: The keykeeper is blind, and sees more than we do. He just will not say.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.candlewife.idle.4: If a candle goes out, do not light it from a hearth. That fire is alive, and they have no use for living things.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.first.0: The door is open, I know. I will not go out. They gave me a hundred days.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.first.1: A hundred days is a hundred sunsets. And there is only the one sunset here, and it does not end. How long have I sat here? Not a day.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.first.2: I am in debt. To whom, I will not say: he died. Though nobody here has properly died.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.overseer.0: The Overseer? He always told me: "Sit till dawn." And I told him: what dawn, open your eyes.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.overseer.1: Well. He did not sit it out.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.chaplain.0: The Chaplain used to come down here and teach us to call the sunset dawn. Those who learnt it got bread.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.mother.0: The one they hanged on the Mire, they brought her here first. The next cell. She said it loud, for the whole ward to hear: "The day must end."
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.mother.1: I kept quiet. I keep quiet altogether. I have my term.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.wharf.0: Down by the sea, they say, there is a real morning. I do not believe it. Morning is when a day comes after it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.coming.0: They say he stopped the day so that tomorrow would not come. What was meant to come, you know better: you went there.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.coming.1: To my mind he stopped it so as not to pay his debts. Tomorrow is when they come to collect.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.started.0: The clock runs? Then so does my term.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.started.1: A hundred days. Never mind. I am used to it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.seat.0: The sunset stands again. And I had just started counting.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.seat.1: Somebody has taken his seat, it seems. What is it to me. I sit anyway.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.idle.0: Leave the door. I did not open it, and it is not mine to close.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.idle.1: The key to the Quarrymen's Gate came up with the last load of stone. They took it on up, to the city. Everything good goes up there.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.idle.2: Sunset. I say sunset. Let them hear.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.idle.3: They fed us while there was something to feed us. Then they stopped. But the hunger did not pass. It is stuck too.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.debtor.idle.4: You owe someone too, I can see it in your eyes. You just do not know whom.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.first.0: Do not stand in my light. There is little enough of it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.first.1: I am carving a face. The Founder's. To be done by dawn, the order was. That is how they said it, "by dawn". So by dawn I am carving it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.first.2: The nose I remember. There was a nose. The rest the stone remembers better than I do, and it will not tell.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.taskmaster: No more Taskmaster? He drove wedges so we would not sleep. A good taskmaster he was.
He did not remember the face either. He kept shouting: "That is it! That is him!"
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.stone_eate: The Stone-Eater lies down. He ate the white stone, the stone for the head. We thought he meant harm.
Or maybe he was just hungry. Everyone here wants something.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.coming.0: You have been under the pit, you say? We drove a gallery down there, after cleaner stone. And we cut through.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.coming.1: There is sky down there, do you understand? Sky, under the ground. The Taskmaster had it barred with a grate and told us to keep quiet.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.coming.2: And I keep quiet. I have only told you.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.started.0: Something knocks underfoot. Steady, like the mallet of a good mason. I never learnt to.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.raised.0: Have you seen the tower? True as a plumb line, not a chip on it. We did not cut it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.seat.0: Dawn again? Good enough. Then it is not too late to finish.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.idle.0: Have you seen the head in the wall? That is us. A hundred men, a hundred days. Only there were no days.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.idle.1: Keep the powder in the pit away from fire. You know that.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.idle.2: If you cannot remember a face, carve your own. Nobody will notice. Once I... No. I will not say.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.idle.3: White stone is soft while it is fresh. And everything is fresh here. Nothing gets old.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.carver.idle.4: The blind ones in the drifts listen. Tread softly, or better, do not tread at all.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.first.0: Take you across? Where to, over what? The water stands, it will not hold a boat, and there is nobody. Sit, since you came.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.first.1: I used to take people to the far bank. The far bank is where this one is now.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.first.2: It is noon here. The sun stopped over the gallows and will not move. The Stockade got the sunset, and we got this.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.wallower: The Wallower lies down. He held the water so it would not sleep. Or it held him.
It may sink a finger now, you will see.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.mother.0: She is down? I saw them hang her. The hangman kept rubbing his hands: the rope will not go, he said. It will not tighten.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.mother.1: Noon stopped, and she stayed as she was. Not alive, and not the other thing either.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.mother.2: She said only one thing: the day must end. I think so too. I just do not say it loud: I have a boat to think of.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.elder.0: The Unsleeping came to the hanging. They stood on the log road and watched. One of them carried the key to their wicket, so nobody would follow them.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.elder.1: He dropped it in the grove and was afraid to go back. They fear noon: noon makes you drowsy.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.helmsman: The helmsman of the Daybreak? I knew him. He asked me out to sea. I said: I am a river man. And he said: what is the difference, the water stands everywhere.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.coming.0: Whatever you did under the ground, I do not know. But the water stirred today. The first time since that noon.
A clock, you say? Then evening is near. I will go and look at the boat.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.seat.0: Noon again. And I had the oars out already. Well, I will put them back.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.idle.0: You see the boat? Tied up. I will not untie it: it would drift off, and where to? Nowhere.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.idle.1: The log roads hold while you keep walking. Do not stand still.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.idle.2: The lights on the marsh are not people. People do not come here.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.idle.3: I would take a soul from you for the crossing. Only there is no crossing. All the ferries are free here, because they go nowhere.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.ferryman.idle.4: They say there is a dawn at the Stockade. I have been there. It is a sunset. Red as the water in a pool.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.first.0: Keep away from the rope. There is a hanging on.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.first.1: It has been on since noon. The order was: hanged by sundown. But there is no sundown, it is dawn, that is what we are to call it. So I am not done.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.first.2: She is out there on her island. Grown over with roots. I wait. A hangman always waits for it to be over.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.mother.0: It is over?.. Well then. The hanging is done.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.mother.1: Do you know the last thing she said to me? "You will see the sunset." There. I see it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.mother.2: I am going. There is nothing for me here any more. Do not touch the rope. It is only a rope now.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.idle.0: She said the day must end. I said it was not for me to decide. So I do not decide.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.idle.1: I changed the rope. Three times. No rope will hold her.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.idle.2: The candlewife in the borough sets a candle for her. For her being hanged. A kind woman.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.hangman.idle.3: Dawn. I say dawn. That is what I was told to say.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.first.1: I keep the count of the days. As many candles burnt, so many nights. That makes three thousand and more. And not once has it grown light over the firs.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.first.2: It does not add up. You are not asleep? Good. Here one must not.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.shatun.0: No more Shatun? They kept him chained at the gate so that he would not sleep either. If we do not sleep, nothing sleeps. I have written: the beast. One line.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.mother.0: Three of ours went to the hanging on the Mire. The Elder sent them to see whether the day would end. It did not.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.mother.1: One of them lost a key, the key of the wicket. I wrote it off as lost.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.elder.0: The Elder has fallen asleep?.. I write: the Elder has fallen asleep. The first entry after which I want to close the book.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.elder.1: He took our vow until the morning. The morning did not come, but the vow is still here. A vow without a morning is only sleeplessness.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.wharf.0: The key to the Sea Gate lay here in the candle store. They brought it from the port for safekeeping: where nobody sleeps, there is the best watch.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.wharf.1: You have been there. What is there?.. No. Do not tell me. I will write that I do not know.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.coming.0: You have killed what was meant to come. Then could the morning have come? Or was the morning what was coming? I am writing it as a question.
The clock runs. I have checked: my count and theirs differ by three thousand days. One of us lies.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.seat.0: It does not grow light over the firs after all. So. Twelve candles a night. Write on.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.idle.0: We take the wax from those who will not get up again. They do not mind. They do not mind anything.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.idle.1: Do not touch the sleep moths. Their dust is sleep, and sleep here is the same as death, only shameful.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.idle.2: The wakers strike anyone who lets his head droop. Me, never. I keep my head in the book.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.cellarer.idle.3: How long have you been here? Tell me, and I will write it down. Every day counts with us, though there are none.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.first.0: Eh? Speak up. I am the bellman. Deaf. All bellmen go deaf who ring long enough.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.first.1: That bell has not struck since that day. I was told to wait. If they tell me to strike, I strike. Have you come to tell me?
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.first.2: What is in the sky out there? I cannot see it from here.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.seat.0: Has somebody sat in the seat? I felt it: the stone shook. Well, then I do not strike.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.seat.1: What is in the sky out there?
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.idle.0: What is in the sky out there?
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.idle.1: The rope is up there. Pull it yourself if you were told to. Nobody tells me anything. I cannot hear.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.idle.2: He used to sit up there, in the seat. Maybe he still does. I would not hear.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.idle.3: If you strike it, I will feel it. You hear a bell with your feet.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.bellman.idle.4: The bell used to call to evensong. There is no evensong now, but there is the bell.

spell.unfading_dawn.heavy_soul_shard.des: Slow and heavy: hits twice as hard
spell.unfading_dawn.fire_orb.desc: A ball of fire that bursts where it lands
spell.unfading_dawn.flare.desc: A tongue of flame three paces from the palm; it goes round a shield
spell.unfading_dawn.soul_scatter.desc: Five shards in a fan: up close all of them land
spell.unfading_dawn.root_snare.desc: A root comes up under whoever you look at: it strikes and holds
spell.unfading_dawn.marsh_fire.desc: A slow flame: it bends its own way to an enemy and burns on it for long
spell.unfading_dawn.dry_wind.desc: A dry wind from the palm: it hurts little, but it throws back what it meets and fans what burns
spell.unfading_dawn.sun_patch.desc: A patch of light where you look: it gathers for a moment, and burns whoever is still in it
spell.unfading_dawn.hot_wax.desc: A gush of wax from the palm: it burns little, but sets on the legs

message.unfading_dawn.gate_locked.quarry: Locked. The stone from here went to the Stockade; so did the key.
message.unfading_dawn.gate_locked.mire: Locked. It smells of the bog under the grate. The key went where nothing lies deeper.
place.unfading_dawn.isle: THE ISLE OF THE WEEPING ONE
message.unfading_dawn.gate_locked.firwoo: Locked. It smells of fir and wax beyond the grate. The key was carried off to a hanging, and never brought back.
message.unfading_dawn.gate_locked.shore: Locked. Salt and tar on the draught under the leaves. The key was kept where nobody sleeps.
message.unfading_dawn.gate_locked.stubbl: Locked. Dry heat and straw on the draught through the grate. The key went down to the sea, to meet those the bread was for.
message.unfading_dawn.undertow: The sea is taking you under
message.unfading_dawn.gate_locked.none: Locked. The key to this lock is not in these parts.
message.unfading_dawn.shard_found: A flask shard. At a hearth it will melt into the flask by itself.

dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.first.0: Steps... Living steps. Nobody has walked here on their own two feet for a long time.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.first.1: I am blind, but I know my keys by touch. This one opens your luck. A joke. Take this instead.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.first.2: Drink from the flask when things get bad. When it is empty, sit by a hearth and it will fill itself.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.first.3: And do not play the hero: the souls you carry stay where you fall. Come back in time and they are yours again.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.0: The Gravedigger still digs in the churchyard. He has laid the whole borough down and cannot stop.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.1: If you hear a watchman's bell, strike him first. Otherwise the whole street comes running.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.2: The hounds are quick but frail. Raise your shield, wait for the leap, then strike.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.3: The guards hide behind their shields. Wait for them to strike, or get behind them.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.4: Roll. At my age it does not work any more, but you are just right for it.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.5: The road past the churchyard leads to the Stockade. Up there the sun will not set, and down here it will not rise.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.6: See it glowing in the ash? That is a flask shard. Pick it up: one more gulp for you.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.7: Spend your souls at a hearth. The dead have no use for them.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.8: The Quarrymen's Gate, at the end of Low Street? Shut since the stone stopped coming. Its key went up to the Stockade with the last load. Not one of mine.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.idle.9: They say there are some in the quarry that have no eyes. Those listen. Go past them creeping.
message.unfading_dawn.clock.filled: A key already lies in this socket
message.unfading_dawn.clock.empty.quarry: The socket bears the quarry's sign. It wants the key to the Quarrymen's Gate
message.unfading_dawn.clock.empty.mire: The socket bears the sign of the mire. It wants the key to the Mire Gate

message.unfading_dawn.clock.empty.shore: The socket bears the sign of the wharf. It wants the key to the Sea Gate
message.unfading_dawn.clock.empty.stubbl: The socket bears the sign of the stubble. It wants the key to the Reapers' Gate
message.unfading_dawn.clock.empty.depths: The socket bears the sign of the depths. It wants the key to the Lower Grate
message.unfading_dawn.clock.empty.keeper: The socket has no sign, only the cut of a key. Such a key is kept in the borough
message.unfading_dawn.clock.set: The key sets into its socket: %s of %s
message.unfading_dawn.clock.started: Something under the ground gave way and began to move. Up in the borough, a tower is rising.
message.unfading_dawn.clock.rope: The rope comes heavy, as if pulled up from under the ground.
message.unfading_dawn.clock.seat_taken: The seat has gone cold and empty
message.unfading_dawn.clock.seat: You sit in the Founder's seat. The stone is warm.
message.unfading_dawn.clock.silence: It has gone quiet. So quiet that you can hear the dead not walking.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.0: The rope comes heavy, and the bell overhead stirs unwillingly.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.1: It has not struck since the day the Founder sat in his seat. It strikes now.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.2: Once. The sunset that stood over the Stockade does not fade; it crumbles like ash.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.3: Twice. Those who held to their feet by stubbornness alone lie down where they stood.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.4: Thrice. The Bellman below lifts his head. "I hear it," he says. "That is all, then."
ending.unfading_dawn.1.5: The day is over. Not at once and not painfully: there is simply nothing left to go on.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.6: And over the sea, where there was nothing, a black disc rises with an amber rim and a crown of hands.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.7: The hands reach down. Not for you. For what is left.
ending.unfading_dawn.1.title: THE END OF THE DAY
ending.unfading_dawn.1.subtitle: The sunset is out.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.0: The seat is stone, and warm. As if someone had just got up.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.1: You sit. The bell overhead does not sway.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.2: The light is the same: the same sunset behind the battlements, the same hush on the stair.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.3: Below, all is as it was: the dead walk, the living fear, the clock ticks under the ground.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.4: From the stair the Bellman asks what is in the sky. He is deaf and will not hear an answer.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.6: There is nothing more to do but sit. The clock runs, and tomorrow will not come.
ending.unfading_dawn.2.title: DAWN
ending.unfading_dawn.2.subtitle: Unfading.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.clock.0: The Coming is down? I heard the ground sigh. Then it is time for me to give up what I kept.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.clock.1: This key opens no gate. It is for the clock that runs beneath your boots. The seventh socket is mine; the other six you gathered yourself.
dialogue.unfading_dawn.keykeeper.clock.2: Set it, and the clock will run. What it raises I cannot say. I am blind, and I never saw towers even when I could.
